evidence.observation: deepMergeObjects/deepMergeSettings define the merge rule used across every scope: overrides win over base, undefined override values are skipped (lines 172-177), and nested plain objects merge recursively while arrays/scalars replace wholesale (isMergeableObject, lines 165-167). deepMergeSettings is the single primitive that composes global and project settings and CLI overrides.

The FileSettingsStorage constructor pins the two persistent scopes to concrete files: global (user) settings at `<agentDir>/settings.json` (line 237) and project settings at `<cwd>/<CONFIG_DIR_NAME>/settings.json`, i.e. `.pi/settings.json` (line 238). This is the physical evidence for the 'user' and 'project' rows of the precedence table.

The class and its private constructor store globalSettings and projectSettings separately and compute the effective settings as `deepMergeSettings(this.globalSettings, this.projectSettings)` (line 350). Because project is passed as the overrides argument, project values outrank user values for every scalar, while nested objects (compaction, retry, terminal, markdown, warnings, images) merge key-by-key.

Project settings are gated on trust: `if (scope === "project" && !projectTrusted) return {}` (lines 411-413), so an untrusted project contributes nothing and user/global settings plus defaults remain in effect. Also shows each scope is parsed independently and migrated (line 424-425).

applyOverrides performs `this.settings = deepMergeSettings(this.settings, overrides)`, layering a runtime (CLI-derived) override on top of the already-merged user+project settings. This is the mechanism that makes CLI flags the highest-precedence level; it is called from main.ts for --use-theme.

Representative default layer: each field is resolved with `??` to a built-in default (maxRetries 3, baseDelayMs 2000, maxAgentDelayMs DEFAULT_MAX_AGENT_RETRY_DELAY_MS). Every typed getter follows this pattern (e.g. getCompactionTokenSetting at 859-885, getTransport at 836-838, getTuiMode at 1265-1267), which is the 'default' row of the precedence table and also validates/normalizes out-of-range values.

Deliberate exception to normal precedence: reads only `this.globalSettings.cacheWarming` (line 956), ignoring project settings because warming costs money, defaulting to "streaming". getDefaultProjectTrust (1031-1034) is likewise global-only. Shows the precedence table has documented per-key opt-outs where project scope is excluded entirely.

Value-level discriminator: a config string starting with `!` is classified as a shell command reference (lines 81-83); anything else is parsed as a template of literal and `$ENV`/`${ENV}` parts (line 85, via parseConfigValueTemplate at 28-78). This chooses which resolution source outranks which for a single value.

Environment precedence for interpolated values: an explicitly supplied `env` record wins (`env?.[name]`), falling back to `process.env[name]`, and returning undefined when neither is set (line 89). resolveTemplate (101-113) then treats any missing referenced variable as an overall resolution failure.

Public entry point for resolving a settings-derived value (API key, header, provider field): command references execute the shell command via executeCommand (cached, 208-216), all other references interpolate the template. Establishes the value precedence: shell command > env interpolation (explicit env > process.env) > literal text.

Failure semantics that complete the precedence story: when a value cannot be resolved it reports the command (lines 236-238) or the specific missing environment variables (240-248), so configuration precedence is observable/diagnosable from error messages rather than silently falling through.

CLI-flag precedence over settings, outside the core directory but the caller that produces the top table row: the explicit `--thinking` value is applied after scoped-model/default thinking (lines 514-517), and `--tools`/`--exclude-tools`/`--no-tools` are written into session options (532-543) ahead of settingsManager defaults. main.ts:796 shows `parsed.models ?? settingsManager.getEnabledModels()` and main.ts:667 shows `applyOverrides({ theme: parsed.useTheme })`.

Defines the user/global scope location used by settings-manager: `~/.pi/agent` (line 533), overridable by the PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR environment variable (lines 529-532). CONFIG_DIR_NAME at line 504 ('.pi', from package.json piConfig, where piConfig.configDir is applied) is what makes the project path `<cwd>/.pi/settings.json`. Explains the directory names in the precedence table.

Built-in default constants for the lowest precedence level. DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL = "medium" is consumed in sdk.ts:237/248 as `settingsManager.getDefaultThinkingLevel() ?? DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL`, confirming the default tier is applied only when neither CLI nor user/project settings supply a value.

claims.claim: Settings are resolved by four ordered scopes, highest to lowest: (1) CLI/runtime overrides applied via SettingsManager.applyOverrides; (2) trusted project settings at <cwd>/.pi/settings.json; (3) user/global settings at ~/.pi/agent/settings.json; (4) built-in defaults supplied by the typed getters (and DEFAULT_* constants).

User and project settings are combined by deepMergeSettings(globalSettings, projectSettings), so project wins for scalars/arrays while nested plain objects merge recursively; undefined override keys never erase a lower-level value.

The CLI tier is realized by applyOverrides merging a parsed-flag object on top of the merged settings, and by explicit CLI flag checks (e.g. parsed.thinking, parsed.tools, parsed.models) that short-circuit the settings getters in buildSessionOptions and main.ts.

Project settings participate only when the project is trusted: loadFromStorage returns an empty object for an untrusted project, so the effective order for untrusted projects collapses to CLI > user > default.
Precedence is per-key, not all-or-nothing: some settings are declared global-only (cacheWarming, defaultProjectTrust) and read only globalSettings, deliberately ignoring any project value.

For individual config values referenced from settings (API keys, headers), resolve-config-value.ts applies its own precedence: a '!'-prefixed value runs as a shell command, otherwise the template is interpolated where an explicit env argument outranks process.env, and a missing environment variable makes the value resolve to undefined (or throw with the variable named).

The lowest tier is a typed default applied with ?? inside each getter (and constants such as DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL), so a value only reaches that tier when it is absent from CLI, project and user scopes.

conclusion:
Precedence table for packages/coding-agent/src/core settings (highest wins):

| Rank | Scope | Source | Evidence symbol | Evidence location |
|------|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
| 1 | CLI / runtime | Parsed CLI flags (--thinking, --tools/--exclude-tools/--no-tools, --models, --use-theme, --session-dir) | SettingsManager.applyOverrides; buildSessionOptions | settings-manager.ts:568-570; main.ts:450-546, 667, 796 |
| 2 | Project | <cwd>/.pi/settings.json (only if project trusted) | FileSettingsStorage (constructor), loadFromStorage | settings-manager.ts:237-238, 410-426 |
| 3 | User | ~/.pi/agent/settings.json (agent dir overridable via PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR) | FileSettingsStorage, getAgentDir | settings-manager.ts:237; config.ts:599-605 |
| 4 | Default | Built-in defaults applied by typed getters and DEFAULT_* constants | getRetrySettings, getCompactionTokenSetting, DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL | settings-manager.ts:932-939, 859-885; defaults.ts:1-11 |

Composition rules: (a) user+project are merged with deepMergeSettings(global, project) in the SettingsManager constructor (settings-manager.ts:350), project acting as the override; nested objects merge recursively and undefined keys are skipped (deepMergeObjects, 169-186); (b) CLI overrides are layered last with applyOverrides (568-570); (c) project scope is dropped entirely when untrusted (410-413); (d) some keys are intentionally global-only, e.g. getCacheWarmingMode (954-958) and getDefaultProjectTrust (1031-1034); (e) defaults/regex validation live inside getters (e.g. getRetrySettings 932-939, getTuiMode 1265-1267).

At the value level inside a setting, resolve-config-value.ts applies: shell command ('!' prefix) > environment interpolation > literal, with an explicit env argument outranking process.env, and unresolved references reported by name (resolveConfigValue 145-151; resolveEnvConfigValue 88-90; resolveConfigValueOrThrow 229-251).
